erin_support: Customer report — rerank returns look wrong: items reordered and scores are huge/odd strings. They say this started after a minor SDK bump. request_id=r-abc123

oliver_ts: Can you paste the exact SDK call they used and a sample response (scrub secrets)?

erin_support: TS snippet they pasted:
```ts
await client.rerank({
  model: 'r-rerank-001',
  input: 'how to reset password',
  candidates: ['Reset password flow','Password policy','Account recovery']
})
```
Server response (from customer):
`candidates: ['Password policy','Reset password flow','Account recovery']`
`scores: ['-0.0000023000000000000002','-0.0000023','-0.0000023000000000000000002']`

devon_js: That looks like the TS client is sending scores as strings (we used to send numbers). If backend expects numbers, downstream sorting/parsing can behave weirdly. Any chance of locale / toLocaleString influence?

li_py: I tried repro with our py SDK quickly using same candidate set — py sends numbers by default. TS wire sample I captured locally shows "scores":["-0.0000023000000000002"] (strings). Repro steps: `node ./repro-ts.js` (attached) -> inspect body in mitmproxy.

beth_eng: Confirmed on my machine. Root cause: when we normalized scores in ts-sdk we inadvertently `String(score.toPrecision(22))` in a helper to keep precision; later code assumed numeric and didn't cast back. So JSON ends up with quoted numbers. Some clients/proxies (and our server strict schema) accept strings; others coerce to weird formats causing ordering/sorting changes.

erin_support: Customer impact: rerank ordering changed in prod for some queries. They're willing to test a patch in staging.

beth_eng: Quick fix: cast to Number right before creating the request body (single-line patch). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ts-sdk/pull/482 (fixes serialization). Added unit test that rejects stringified scores.

release-bot: Patch release queued to canary (build 2023.11.7-rc1).

oliver_ts: I'll follow up with the customer, advise immediate workaround: pin to ts-sdk vX.Y.Z-previous or use py sdk as a short-term mitigation. Also note we should add a server-side validation to reject string scores early with a clear error.

erin_support: Thanks — passing to customer, will post acceptance once they validate staging. :thumbsup:
